explanation: King Solomon of Israel, who is believed to be the author of Song of Songs and regarded as a wise man in the Bible.
The woman mentioned in Song of Songs, loved by the bridegroom. In an allegorical interpretation, the bride often represents God's people or the church.
The man who expresses his love for the bride in Song of Songs. In an allegorical interpretation, he often represents God or Jesus Christ.
A deep devotion, passion, and tenderness between two people. The love between the bride and the bridegroom in Song of Songs often symbolizes God's love for His people.
A place where the bride and bridegroom meet and share their love. The garden can also symbolize paradise and harmony between God and humanity.
A time of year when nature awakens to life again after winter. Spring often symbolizes renewal, rebirth, and a new beginning.
A swift and graceful animal frequently mentioned in Song of Songs. The gazelle symbolizes beauty, grace, and freedom.
